questions.questionText:
**Passage:**
The school library had been neglected for several years. Books were dusty, some shelves were broken and many learners preferred to spend their free time outside. A new librarian decided to change the situation. She organised the books, repaired the shelves with the help of the school maintenance team and started a reading club. Within a few months, learners were borrowing books regularly and discussing stories during break time.

Read the passage carefully. Answer the questions that follow. Passage 1.
- (a) Give one reason why the learners initially avoided the library. [1 mark]
- (b) State two actions taken by the new librarian. [2 marks]
- (c) What evidence shows that the changes were successful? [2 marks]
- (d) Give a suitable title for the passage. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) The books were dusty and some shelves were broken [1 mark].
(b) She organised the books, repaired the shelves, and started a reading club (any two) [2 marks].
(c) Learners began borrowing books regularly and discussing stories during break time [2 marks].
(d) Example: "Reviving the School Library" / "The New Librarian" [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Rewrite the sentence in the plural: 'The child carried a box to the classroom.'
- (a) Rewrite the sentence correctly in the plural. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: The children carried boxes to the classrooms [2 marks]. ("child" → "children"; "a box" → "boxes"; "classroom" → "classrooms")

questions.questionText:
Correct the error in the sentence: 'Neither of the boys have completed the task.'
- (a) Write the corrected sentence. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: Corrected sentence: Neither of the boys has completed the task [2 marks]. ("Neither" takes a singular verb "has", not "have".)

questions.questionText:
Join the sentences using 'although': 'The road was muddy. The bus continued its journey.'
- (a) Write one correct combined sentence. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: Although the road was muddy, the bus continued its journey [2 marks]. (OR: The bus continued its journey although the road was muddy.)

questions.questionText:
Rewrite the sentence in the past tense: 'The learners clean the classroom every Friday.'
- (a) Write the sentence in the past tense. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: The learners cleaned the classroom every Friday [2 marks]. ("clean" → past tense "cleaned")

questions.questionText:
Replace the underlined noun phrase with a suitable pronoun: 'Rudo and Chipo carried the books.'
- (a) Rewrite the sentence using an appropriate pronoun. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: They carried the books [2 marks]. ("Rudo and Chipo" is a plural subject → pronoun "They".)

questions.questionText:
Rewrite using 'not only...but also': 'The club teaches reading. The club teaches writing.'
- (a) Write the combined sentence. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: The club teaches not only reading but also writing [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Change the direct speech into reported speech: 'I am ready,' Tendai said.
- (a) Write the sentence in reported speech. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: Tendai said that he (or she) was ready [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Add the missing punctuation: 'what a beautiful garden said the visitor'
- (a) Rewrite the sentence with correct punctuation. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: "What a beautiful garden!" said the visitor [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Give an antonym for the underlined word: 'The water was shallow.'
- (a) Write the opposite of 'shallow'. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: Antonym (opposite) of "shallow": deep [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Give a synonym for the underlined word: 'The villagers were delighted.'
- (a) Write one word with a similar meaning to 'delighted'. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: pleased / overjoyed / happy / thrilled [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Write a friendly letter to a cousin describing a memorable school event.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Friendly letter mark scheme: Sender's address & date [3]; Salutation [1]; Engaging paragraphs describing the memorable event (who, what, where, feelings) [14]; Warm sign-off [2]; Accurate grammar, spelling, and punctuation [5]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a formal letter to the head of your school suggesting two ways of improving the school grounds.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Formal letter mark scheme: Two addresses & date [4]; Formal salutation (Dear Sir/Madam) & underlined heading (RE: IMPROVING SCHOOL GROUNDS) [3]; Two well-explained practical suggestions with reasons [12]; Formal close (Yours faithfully + full name) [2]; Register & accuracy [4]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a story beginning with: 'When I opened the old wooden box, I could not believe what I saw.'
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Narrative composition mark scheme: Exact opening sentence used smoothly [2]; Vivid setting, plot build-up, climax of discovery, and satisfying resolution [15]; Expressive vocabulary, dialogue/sensory details, and clean paragraphing [8]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a composition on: 'The importance of keeping our community clean.'
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Discursive/expository essay mark scheme: Clear introduction defining clean environment [4]; Body paragraphs covering health benefits, prevention of disease/pollution, civic pride, and practical school/community actions [15]; Strong conclusion & grammatical accuracy [6]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a story ending with: 'From that day onwards, I understood the value of telling the truth.'
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Narrative essay mark scheme: Realistic storyline showing temptation/mistake, consequences of dishonesty, and lesson learned [16]; Ending seamlessly with the given sentence [2]; Cohesive paragraphs & accurate mechanics [7]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write an article for your school magazine about responsible use of mobile phones.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Magazine article mark scheme: Catchy title & byline [3]; Balanced points on educational benefits vs distractions/cyber-risks + practical rules for learners [15]; Lively semi-formal tone & strong conclusion [7]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a dialogue between two learners planning a community clean-up campaign.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Dialogue mark scheme: Brief scene-setting; speaker names on left margin with colons (no quotation marks needed); natural exchange planning tools, date, roles, and awareness [18]; Accurate punctuation & register [7]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a speech to your school assembly on the importance of reading.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Speech mark scheme: Formal greeting (Head, teachers, fellow learners) [3]; Engaging hook and persuasive points on vocabulary, exam success, and imagination [15]; Memorable closing call to action & rhetorical flow [7]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a report on a school sports day held at your school.
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Report mark scheme: Heading (TO, FROM, DATE, SUBJECT) [4]; Objective factual account of date, events, house results, guest of honour, and recommendations [15]; Formal past-tense register & accuracy [6]. Total: [25 marks].

questions.questionText:
Write a composition entitled: 'A journey I will never forget.'
- (a) Write your response in continuous prose, observing appropriate structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation. [25 marks]
questions.explanation: Descriptive/narrative essay mark scheme: Destination and purpose [4]; Vivid chronological details of travel, sights, unexpected incident, and feelings [14]; Varied sentence structures & accurate spelling [7]. Total: [25 marks].
